blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) localizes the image region described by a natural language expression, underpinning applications such as autonomous navigation, human-robot interaction, and medical image analysis. Under weak supervision, REC is challenged by the visual-linguistic semantic gap and the difficulty of inferring region-text correspondences from coarse image-level signals alone. Moreover, no single visual encoder captures all complementary properties---semantic alignment, fine-grained texture, and boundary awareness---while naively fusing multiple pretrained encoders yields heterogeneous, hard-to-reconcile representations. We propose LaMER, a weakly supervised REC framework that dynamically aggregates four frozen expert encoders through a language-conditioned Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module, adapting expert selection to each referring expression without instance-level bounding-box supervision. A Cell-Text Matching Head with Negative Anchor Augmentation, trained with a multi-objective loss combining contrastive, reconstruction, alignment, and load-balancing terms, further stabilizes optimization. LaMER achieves 77.67\%, 62.81\%, and 69.49\% Acc@IoU\(\geq 0.5\) on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, surpassing DViN and WeakMCN by up to 16.49 and 14.49 points, with ablations validating each component.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Understanding and localizing natural language references to visual
content is a core requirement for intelligent systems operating in
the real world. Referring Expression Comprehension (REC), the task
of localizing the image region described by a natural language
expression, underpins applications such as autonomous
navigation ( Deruyttere et al., 2019 ) , human-robot
interaction ( Shridhar et al., 2020 ) , and medical image
analysis ( Lei et al., 2023 ) , where systems must identify the
target object among multiple visually similar candidates.

blocks.en:
REC remains fundamentally challenged by a visual-linguistic semantic
gap between continuous visual representations and discrete language
tokens, an absence of instance-level supervision, and the difficulty
of integrating heterogeneous visual representations. These
challenges intensify under weak supervision, where models learn
solely from image-level signals, making the quality of visual
representations the primary bottleneck: features must be both
spatially discriminative and semantically aligned with the language
query. Yet no single visual encoder simultaneously captures all
complementary visual cues—semantic alignment, fine-grained
texture, structure, and boundary awareness. Integrating multiple
specialized pretrained encoders through a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
paradigm ( Shazeer et al., 2017 ) is a promising direction, but
heterogeneous experts produce representations optimized for
different objectives and feature distributions, making naive fusion
ineffective; a learned language-conditioned router further risks
collapsing onto a small subset of experts without appropriate
load-balancing regularization.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work and Preliminaries
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作和初步情况

blocks.en: 2.1 Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
blocks.zh: 2.1 开放词汇 对象检测

blocks.en: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) extends detection beyond predefined categories to novel concepts described through natural language. Early semantic-transfer approaches were limited by weak visual-semantic alignment; large-scale vision-language pretraining (e.g., CLIP, ALIGN) improved this via contrastive learning on image-text pairs. Building on such models, ViLD ( Gu et al., 2022 ) distills a frozen CLIP teacher into a detector; GLIP and RegionCLIP reformulate detection as phrase grounding; YOLO-World ( Cheng et al., 2024 ) introduces a lightweight vision-language pathway for real-time inference. Despite these advances, OVD models remain designed for category-level recognition and are insufficient for compositional expressions involving attributes, spatial relationships, and context—so directly applying OVD representations to REC remains challenging.
blocks.zh: Open-vocabulary对象检测(OVD)将检测范围超越了预先定义的类别,扩展到通过自然语言描述的新概念. 早期的语义移位方法受到视觉语义对齐性弱的限制;大规模视觉语言预训(如CLIP,ALIGN)通过在图像文本对子上的对比性学习来改进了这一点. 在这些模型的基础上,ViLD(Gu等人,2022年)将冷冻的CLIP教师蒸馏成探测器;GLIP和RegionCLIP重排检测作为词组落地;YOLO-World(Cheng等人,2024年)引入了轻量级视觉语言路径进行实时推断. 尽管取得了这些进展,但OVD模型仍然用于类别一级的识别,不足以用于涉及属性、空间关系和上下文的构成表达——因此,将OVD表述直接应用于REC仍然具有挑战性。

blocks.en: 2.2 Referring Expression Comprehension
blocks.zh: 2.2 参照表达式理解

blocks.en: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) aims to localize the image region described by a natural language expression, requiring models to identify the intended instance among visually similar candidates. Existing approaches divide into fully supervised and weakly supervised paradigms.
blocks.zh: 转介表达理解(REC)旨在将自然语言表达描述的图像区域本地化,要求模型在视觉上相似的候选者中识别预期实例. 现有办法分为全面监督和监督不力的模式。

blocks.en:
Early REC approaches relied on modular architectures that decomposed
expressions into semantic components such as object categories,
attributes, and spatial relationships ( Yu et al., 2018 ; Hu et al., 2017 ) ,
while graph-based methods modeled objects as nodes and exploited
relational reasoning over scene
structures ( Wang et al., 2019 ; Yang et al., 2020 ) . With
Transformer-based vision-language architectures, approaches such as
TransVG ( Deng et al., 2021 ) , MDETR ( Kamath et al., 2021 ) , and
SeqTR ( Choi et al., 2022 ) achieved strong performance through
end-to-end cross-modal interaction and localization, but their
dependence on expensive instance-level bounding-box annotations
limits scalability to large-scale scenarios ( Liu et al., 2019a ) .

blocks.en: 3 Proposed Method
blocks.zh: 3 拟议方法

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 概览

blocks.en: LaMER couples a YOLO11x-based visual encoder ( Khanam and Hussain, 2024 ) and a Bi-GRU language encoder with a Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module that assigns soft weights to four frozen expert encoders and dynamically mixes them with the backbone feature through a learnable residual gate, strengthening cross-modal alignment under weak supervision.
blocks.zh: LaMER与一个基于YOLO11x的视觉编码器(Khanam和Hussain,2024年)和一个带有跨Modal Routing Fusion模块的Bi-GRU语言编码器对4个冷冻专家编码器进行软重分配,并通过一个可学习的剩余门将其与骨干特性动态混合,在薄弱的监督下加强跨模式对接.

blocks.en: The fused representation is subsequently processed by the Cell-Text Matching Head, which performs region-text alignment through anchor-level contrastive matching. Negative Anchor Augmentation adds challenging negatives during training to improve discrimination, and LaMER is optimized with a multi-objective loss combining contrastive, reconstruction, alignment, and load-balancing objectives, enabling stable routing without instance-level bounding-box annotations.

blocks.zh: 3.3 拟议系统架构

blocks.en: Figure 1: Overall architecture of the proposed LaMER framework.
blocks.zh: 图 1: 拟议的LAMER框架的总体结构。

blocks.en:
As illustrated in Figure 1 , the system consists of five components: the YOLO11x visual encoder, the Bi-GRU language encoder, the Expert Feature Bank, the Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module, and the Cell-Text Matching Head. The input image I ∈ ℝ H × W × 3 I\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times 3} and referring expression Q = { w 1 , … , w T } Q=\{w_{1},\ldots,w_{T}\} are fed in parallel into the visual and language encoders, extracting multi-scale visual features and a 512-dimensional context-aware language representation. These visual features are enriched by four frozen experts in the Expert Feature Bank—SigLIP SO400M ( Zhai et al., 2023 ) , DINOv2 ViT-L/14 ( Oquab et al., 2023 ) , EfficientSAM (ViT-T) ( Xiong et al., 2024 ) , and ConvNeXt-B ( Liu et al., 2022b ) —each projected to a common 13 × 13 13\times 13 , 1024-channel resolution. The Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module weights each expert’s contribution by conditioning on a joint visual-linguistic query, producing a fused
visual feature passed to the Cell-Text Matching Head, which selects
the top- K K cells by objectness, matches them against the query, and produces the final bounding box b ^ = ( x , y , w , h ) \hat{b}=(x,y,w,h) without bounding-box supervision during training.

blocks.en: 3.3.1 Data Preprocessing
blocks.zh: 3.3.1 国家 数据处理

blocks.en: This stage converts raw image–text pairs from the RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg datasets ( Yu et al., 2016 ; Mao et al., 2016 ; Kazemzadeh et al., 2014 ) into a format suitable for the encoding and grounding modules; consistent with the weakly supervised setting, ground-truth boxes are withheld during training and used only for evaluation. Images are resized to 416 × 416 416\times 416 pixels for the YOLO11x backbone, and each of the four expert encoders receives its own resolution- and normalization-matched view, since they were pretrained under different conventions; full per-branch preprocessing values are given in Appendix B . We tokenize each referring expression into GloVe ( Pennington et al., 2014 ) word-index sequences, padded or truncated to T max = 15 T_{\max}=15 tokens.

blocks.en: 3.3.2 Feature Extraction
blocks.zh: 3.3.2 提取特征

blocks.en: Three parallel branches process the preprocessed image and referring expression, producing the visual and linguistic representations that the Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module consumes.
blocks.zh: 三个平行分支处理预处理的图像和转录表达方式,产生跨模组循环融合模块所消耗的视觉和语言表现.

blocks.en:
YOLO11x ( Khanam and Hussain, 2024 ) serves as the primary visual encoder, chosen for its ability to jointly produce region proposals and semantically rich multi-scale features within a single backbone. It builds hierarchical representations through C3k2 blocks with progressively larger receptive fields, an SPPF layer, and a C2PSA (Cross-Stage Partial with Spatial Attention) module at its final stage; the backbone is kept frozen except for C2PSA, which is selectively unfrozen so its spatial attention can adapt to the grounding task without disturbing the earlier general-purpose layers. The encoder outputs three feature maps at different spatial scales— f L ∈ ℝ B × 1024 × 13 × 13 f_{L}\in\mathbb{R}^{B\times 1024\times 13\times 13} , f M ∈ ℝ B × 512 × 26 × 26 f_{M}\in\mathbb{R}^{B\times 512\times 26\times 26} , and f S ∈ ℝ B × 256 × 52 × 52 f_{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{B\times 256\times 52\times 52} —and objectness scores from the frozen detection heads serve as the anchor candidates used in Section 3.3.3 .
The referring expression is encoded with a Bidirectional GRU (Bi-GRU) over frozen GloVe ( Pennington et al., 2014 ) word embeddings (300-dimension), chosen so that spatial modifiers common in referring expressions (e.g., “on the left”) are contextualized using information from both directions rather than only after the head noun. Each direction maintains a 256-dimension hidden state; the concatenated forward/backward outputs form a 512-dimension contextual token representation, further refined by three layers of multi-head self-attention and compressed by attention-based pooling into a global language feature f lang ∈ ℝ B × 512 f_{\text{lang}}\in\mathbb{R}^{B\times 512} .
Following preprocessing (Section 3.3.1 ), each of the four frozen experts in the Expert Feature Bank — SigLIP SO400M ( Zhai et al., 2023 ) , DINOv2 ViT-L/14 ( Oquab et al., 2023 ) , EfficientSAM (ViT-T) ( Xiong et al., 2024 ) , and ConvNeXt-B ( Liu et al., 2022b ) — produces a complementary representation covering cross-modal semantic alignment, fine-grained self-supervised structure, boundary-aware localization, and local texture, respectively, each projected to 1024 channels and spatially aligned to 13 × 13 13\times 13 to match f L f_{L} .

blocks.en: The Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module integrates the multi-scale YOLO11x features with the four expert representations under a joint visual-linguistic query, operating in four stages: multi-modal fusion, cross-attention routing, expert fusion with dynamic mixing, and top-k cell selection.

blocks.en: 4.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: 4.1 数据集

blocks.en: We evaluate on three standard REC benchmarks: RefCOCO and RefCOCO+ ( Yu et al., 2016 ) , both built on MS-COCO train2014 images via the interactive ReferItGame protocol ( Kazemzadeh et al., 2014 ) and split following the UNC convention (testA: person queries, testB: non-person queries), and RefCOCOg ( Mao et al., 2016 ) , collected non-interactively via Amazon Mechanical Turk ( Amazon Web Services, 2005 ) with longer, more descriptive expressions (8.4 words on average vs. 3.5 for RefCOCO), split following the UMD convention. RefCOCO+ additionally prohibits spatial terms (e.g., “left”/“right”), isolating appearance-based grounding. Table 1 summarizes dataset statistics; Appendix B provides full per-dataset details.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: This work presents LaMER, a weakly supervised REC framework that aggregates complementary visual representations in a query-adaptive manner without instance-level supervision. It couples a YOLO11x visual encoder and a Bi-GRU language encoder with an Expert Feature Bank of four frozen encoders via a Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module and a Cell-Text Matching Head with Negative Anchor Augmentation. Trained end-to-end with a multi-objective loss, LaMER achieves 77.67%, 62.81%, and 69.49% Acc@IoU ≥ 0.5 \geq 0.5 on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, surpassing DViN and WeakMCN by up to +16.49% and +14.49%, with ablations confirming each component’s contribution. Future work includes extending LaMER to weakly supervised Referring Expression Segmentation and exploring adaptive sparse expert routing to reduce inference overhead.
blocks.zh: 这项工作介绍了LaMER,这是一个受到薄弱监督的REC框架,它以可调适的查询方式汇总了互补的视觉表现,而没有实例一级的监督。 它将一个YOLO11x视觉编码器和一个Bi-GRU语言编码器与由四个冷冻编码器组成的专家特性库通过一个跨Modal Routing Fusion模块和一个Cell-Text匹配头与负Anchor增量组合在一起。 LaMER以多重目标亏损的方式,在RefCOCO、RefCO+和RefCOCOg上分别实现了77.67%、62.81%和69.49%的Acc@IoU 0.5\geq 0.5,超过了DViN和弱兆CN,分别达到+16.49%和+14.49%,同时证实了每个组件的贡献。 今后的工作包括:将LaMER扩展至监督不力的“参考表达”分区,探索适应性差的专家路径,以减少推论间接费用。

Attention mechanisms model dependencies within or between sequences
by computing relevance scores between queries and key-value
pairs, dispensing with recurrence to enable parallel
computation [ 45 ] . Scaled Dot-Product Attention
computes a weighted sum of values based on query-key similarity,
while Multi-Head Attention runs several such operations in parallel
across distinct learned subspaces, allowing the model to jointly
attend to different types of relationships within the input. LaMER
uses both mechanisms directly: scaled dot-product attention forms the
basis of the Cross-Attention Router (Section 3.3.3 ), and
multi-head self-attention refines the language representation
(Section 3.3.1 ). Several of LaMER’s frozen expert
encoders also build on the closely related Vision Transformer
architecture [ 46 ] : the Segment Anything
Model [ 47 ] uses a ViT image encoder pretrained via
Masked Autoencoders [ 48 ] to produce spatially rich
embeddings, while DINO-ViT [ 49 ] uses self-supervised
distillation to learn structural, label-free visual representations.
LaMER leverages both properties through its EfficientSAM and DINOv2
experts, respectively.

blocks.en: B.1 Dataset Details
blocks.zh: B.1 数据集细节

blocks.en: RefCOCO [ 31 ] is built on the MS-COCO train2014 image collection, collected through the ReferItGame [ 33 ] platform, an interactive two-player game in which one annotator describes a target object while the other identifies it. The dataset contains 142,210 referring expressions over 50,000 annotated objects across 19,994 images, with an average expression length of 3.5 words. Following the standard UNC split, the data is divided into 120,624 training, 10,834 validation, 5,657 testA, and 5,095 testB expressions. TestA contains expressions referring exclusively to people, while testB covers all other object categories.
blocks.zh: RefCOCO [31] 建在MS-COCO列车2014图像集上,通过ReferenceItGame [33]平台收集,这是一款互动双玩家游戏,其中一名注释者描述一个目标对象,而另一名则识别它. 该数据集包含142,210个引用的表达式超过5万个注释对象,覆盖19,994个图像,平均表达长度为3.5字. 在标准UNC拆分后,数据分为120,624个训练,10,834个验证,5,657个测试A,5,095个测试. B表达法. TestA 包含专指人的表达式, 而测试 B涵盖所有其他对象类别.

blocks.en: RefCOCO+ [ 31 ] shares the same images and collection protocol as RefCOCO but explicitly prohibits spatial location terms such as “left” or “right,” requiring annotators to rely purely on appearance-based cues such as color, texture, and category. The dataset contains 141,564 expressions over 49,856 objects across 19,992 images, with an average query length of 3.53 words, and follows the same UNC split structure as RefCOCO: 120,191 training, 10,758 validation, 5,726 testA, and 4,889 testB expressions.
blocks.zh: RefCOCO+ [31] 与RefCOCO共享相同的图像和收集协议,但明确禁止“左”或“右”等空间位置术语,要求注释者完全依赖外观提示,如颜色、纹理和类别。 该数据集包含141,564个表达式,超过49,856个对象,覆盖19,992个图像,平均查询长度为3.53字,并遵循与RefCOCO相同的UNC分裂结构:120,191个训练,10,758个验证,5,726个测试A,以及4,889个测试. B表达法.

blocks.en: RefCOCOg [ 32 ] is also built on MS-COCO train2014 images, but is collected non-interactively through Amazon Mechanical Turk [ 38 ] rather than a two-player game, resulting in longer and more descriptive expressions. The dataset contains 95,010 expressions over 49,822 objects across 25,799 images , with an average expression length of 8.4 words. Unlike the other two datasets, RefCOCOg does not use a testA/testB split; following the UMD partition, it uses a single, undivided test set that ensures no image appears in more than one subset.
blocks.zh: RefCOCOg [32] 也是在MS-COCO train2014图像上建构的,但通过Amazon Machanical Turk [38] 而非双玩家游戏来进行非交互收集,从而产生更长和更多的描述性表达. 数据集包含95,010个表达式,超过49,822个对象,覆盖25,799个图像,平均表达长度为8.4字. 与另外两个数据集不同,RefCOCOg不使用测试A/testB拆分;在UMD分区之后,它使用一个单一的,未分割的测试集,确保图像不出现在一个以上的子集中.

blocks.en: Table 5 evaluates individual and combined expert configurations. Used in isolation, every expert encoder underperforms the YOLO11x baseline on RefCOCO (67.21% val), with DINOv2 ViT-L achieving the strongest single-encoder result at 60.30%; CLIP alone yields only 37.51%, indicating that a single cross-modal encoder is insufficient for the fine-grained localization required under weak supervision. Progressively combining experts with YOLO11x yields consistent, substantial gains: adding DINOv2 ViT-L alone raises RefCOCO val from 67.21% to 74.23%, and subsequent additions of SigLIP and EfficientSAM further improve performance to 76.37% and 76.87%. Including ConvNeXt-B as the fourth expert reaches the full LaMER configuration at 77.67% on RefCOCO val and 62.81% on RefCOCO+ val, indicating that each expert contributes incremental, complementary information rather than redundant signal.

blocks.en: Table 6 varies the number of experts retained by the router at inference. Restricting the model to a single expert collapses performance to 38.06% and 29.15% on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+ val, far below any multi-expert configuration, confirming that cross-expert complementarity, rather than any individual encoder, drives the routing mechanism’s effectiveness. Expanding to Top-2 recovers most of the gap (75.48% and 59.27%), and performance continues to improve monotonically through Top-3 and Top-4, with larger gains on RefCOCO+ than RefCOCO from Top-2 onward. This monotonic trend indicates that soft attention-based routing continues to extract complementary information as more experts are made available, without the diminishing returns typically associated with hard, single-expert selection.
